title: EPA Risk Management Program as chemical-accident prevention and emergency-preparedness rail
summary: EPA RMP is encoded as a chemical-accident-prevention and emergency-preparedness rail: facilities using extremely hazardous substances develop RMPs, resubmit on a cycle, and expose certain information surfaces. Current rulemaking motion makes this a living regulatory surface.

place.scope: United States / professional process-safety infrastructure unless otherwise stated

claims.claim: EPA says the RMP rule implements Clean Air Act section 112(r) to improve chemical accident prevention and requires facilities using extremely hazardous substances to develop a Risk Management Plan.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: EPA’s RMP page says regulated facilities revise and resubmit RMPs every five years, and that the public can access or request certain RMP information.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: EPA’s current RMP page records a live/current regulatory-motion surface: a 2026 proposed rule to revise RMP, a safer-communities revision note, and a General Duty Clause safety-responsibility surface.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

limitations: Does not establish completeness, compliance, adoption, or effectiveness.
